Welcome to Horizons Therapeutic Education Trust
At the heart of HTET is our commitment to providing profoundly personalised, therapeutic education for children and young people with complex needs, many of whom have experienced significant challenges in accessing and sustaining education. What makes us distinctive is the ambition to genuinely integrate education, care and clinical expertise, rather than seeing these as separate services. Relationships, emotional safety, belonging and understanding each child's individual circumstances are central to our approach.
Our ambition is that every learner leaves HTET safer, more confident, more literate, better qualified and increasingly able to participate in education, community life, training or employment. Success will look different for each young person, but every pathway will be purposeful, ambitious and shaped towards a sustainable next step.

pageCache.text:
The HTET Way
Our vision in practice
Every young person deserves to feel safe, belong, learn and believe in a future beyond their current circumstances. The HTET Way is how we create the relationships, opportunities and personalised pathways that make this possible. We combine compassion with high expectations so that understanding barriers never becomes a reason to limit a young person’s future.
Our shared promise to young people
We will see you. We will listen to you. We will keep you safe. We will not give up on your education or your future. We will help you understand your strengths, overcome barriers and take the next step when you are ready. We will be honest, consistent and ambitious with you and we will celebrate every meaningful step forward.

What We Do
What we do
At Horizons Therapeutic Education Trust, we provide therapeutic education to support children in Somerset. The needs and experiences of this cohort are set out in detail below. Our pupils are children who live in the Homes and Horizons foster homes and children’s homes, as well as a small group of children identified by Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS)
Our unique schools provide the following:
Quality full time education for Somerset’s young people with complex needs.
An innovative curriculum model, designed and delivered by teachers with specialist educational needs/complex needs experience, to engage children and re-introduce them to full time education – often after significant periods of absence.
Strong partnership working between education, health, and social care to truly support Somerset’s most vulnerable children.
Somerset CAMHS will directly deliver therapeutic services and the young people will benefit from the expertise of an in school Therapeutic Lead, Principal Psychologist, Senior Psychologists, Assistant Psychologists, and Sensory Integration Trained Occupational Therapist (OT). In addition to this, the school also has Speech and Language Therapists (SALT), an Art Psychotherapist and Environmental Art Therapist.
Horizons Therapeutic Education Trust is a state-funded alternative provision academy trust, operating learning centres at Misterton and Wellington. The Trust works collaboratively within the wider Homes and Horizons partnership, alongside Somerset Council, Somerset NHS Foundation Trust and Homes2Inspire. Each organisation brings its own expertise and responsibilities to supporting children and young people across Somerset, with HTET retaining independent governance and accountability for its educational provision.

Curriculum
Our curriculum is the route through which hope becomes knowledge, confidence, achievement and opportunity. A strong curriculum is more than a sequence of content; it is a carefully designed pathway that enables each individual to develop and retain powerful knowledge over time. Drawing on evidence from the Education Endowment Foundation (EEF) and wider research into learning, memory and curriculum design, effective curricula are coherent, deliberately sequenced and underpinned by clear disciplinary thinking. They are shaped by what we know about how pupils learn, including the importance of prior knowledge, retrieval, explicit instruction and opportunities to apply learning in meaningful contexts.
The principles outlined below are intended to ensure that our curriculum is ambitious, inclusive and knowledge-rich, providing all learners with equitable access to the cultural capital, understanding and skills they need to succeed in further study, employment and life. These principles serve as the foundation for curriculum planning, implementation and evaluation, ensuring that evidence-informed practice translates into exceptional learning experiences and outcomes for every young person.
Principles
What and Why
Key knowledge is the carefully selected knowledge, concepts, vocabulary and understanding that pupils need to secure to access future learning, make sense of the world and achieve success beyond school. As a key curriculum principle, it provides a clear and coherent foundation for learning, ensuring that the most important content is prioritised, sequenced coherently, revisited and retained over time. A focus on key knowledge helps mitigate the impact of disrupted education, builds confidence through secure understanding, and ensures that essential learning is not left to chance but is deliberately taught, reinforced and applied across the curriculum.
Regulation, Relationships and Communication
Regulation, relationships and communication are fundamental to pupils’ ability to feel safe, engage in learning, express themselves and build positive connections with others. As a key curriculum principle, these capacities are developed intentionally through predictable routines, trusted relationships, explicit teaching and repeated opportunities for supported practice across the curriculum. For HTET pupils, this recognises that learning and wellbeing are interconnected and that progress may depend on pupils gradually developing the strategies, language and confidence needed to manage their responses and participate with others. Through a consistent and personalised approach, the curriculum enables pupils to become increasingly able to communicate their needs, navigate relationships and engage successfully in school and beyond.
Literacy and Numeracy
Literacy and numeracy are the essential communication and mathematical skills that enable pupils to access the curriculum, understand the world around them, solve problems and participate confidently in everyday life. As a key curriculum principle, they provide the foundation for success across all subjects and support pupils to become independent learners. A strong focus on literacy and numeracy is particularly important because disrupted education can create gaps in these fundamental skills, limiting access to wider learning. By prioritising their development across the curriculum, we enable pupils to build confidence, overcome barriers to achievement and access greater opportunities in education, employment and adult life.
Evidence-informed means that curriculum design, teaching approaches and educational decisions are shaped by the best available research, professional expertise and knowledge of pupils' needs. As a key curriculum principle, it ensures that decisions are based on what is known to improve learning rather than on assumption or tradition alone. An evidence-informed approach, from the Education Endowment Foundation for example, is particularly important at HTET because it enables staff to draw on established research relating to learning, memory, attachment, trauma and effective intervention, ensuring that curriculum implementation is responsive, inclusive and more likely to secure positive academic and personal outcomes.
Profoundly Personalised, Adapted, and Accessible
A profoundly personalised and accessible curriculum is designed to meet pupils' individual needs, strengths and starting points while ensuring that all learners can successfully engage with and make progress through the learning on offer. As a key curriculum principle, it recognises that equity is achieved not by treating every pupil the same, but by providing the appropriate support, adaptations and opportunities needed for each learner to succeed. For HTET pupils, a personalised and accessible curriculum is particularly important because it responds to the impact of disrupted education, attachment needs and varying levels of prior learning, ensuring that barriers to participation are reduced and that every pupil can access a broad, ambitious and meaningful curriculum.
Cultural capital is the knowledge, experiences and understanding that broaden pupils' horizons, strengthen their sense of identity and belonging, and equip them to access opportunities, make informed choices and thrive in adult life. As a key curriculum principle, it helps address inequalities in experience and opportunity, ensuring that our pupils develop the confidence, aspirations and social understanding needed to participate fully in society and achieve success beyond their immediate circumstances.
Continuous Development
Continuous development means that the curriculum, and the pupils it serves, are never viewed as finished products but as areas for ongoing growth, reflection and improvement. As a key curriculum principle, it ensures that learning is progressive, responsive and regularly refined through assessment, professional evaluation and an understanding of pupils' changing needs. For HTET, continuous development is particularly important because progress may not always be linear and barriers to learning can change over time. By maintaining a culture of continual review, adaptation and ambition, the curriculum supports sustained academic, personal and social development, ensuring that every pupil can build on prior success and move confidently towards positive future outcomes.

Safeguarding
Any safeguarding concerns should be reported to a member of the Designated Safeguarding Team (DST) immediately who will deal with the concerns and inform the Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL).
The Designated Safeguarding Team can be contacted via email at safeguarding@horizonstet.co.uk.
If anything worries you or concerns you, report it straight away.
If you think someone is in immediate danger please call the Police on 999.
Claire Hudson is our designated Trustee for Safeguarding.
